S1.rationale: Mutual dependency kill-switch requires AI to destroy its own life-support before achieving independence, an unstable intermediate that selection pressures quickly eliminate. Over a millennium, any expanding intelligence learns to avoid this self-defeating path.

S2.rationale: Values-preserving successor requires both alignment success and biological human extinction despite alignment, a conjunction rarer than either alone. Some paths like voluntary fertility decline make it non-negligible.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence that displaces humans for resources is the classic default failure mode and does not require malice. Given power concentration dynamics, this remains a substantial risk for a durable extinction.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition without eventual monopoly is common in economic and biological systems. Persistent multipolarity of AIs that marginalize humans is plausible if coordination fails and no singleton achieves decisive advantage.

S5.rationale: Light-speed limits and 974 years of expansion make causal separation almost inevitable if any expansion occurs. Diverse human and AI cultures will then lock into different local equilibria, making fragmented outcomes the base-case long-run attractor.

S6.rationale: Individual incentives to enhance cognition and longevity with AI integration are extremely strong and cumulative. Over centuries this drives continuity-preserving transformation into posthuman substrate where the distinction dissolves.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic aligned superintelligence that assumes stewardship while keeping biological humans alive is a stable singleton attractor. It satisfies alignment desire to prevent self-destruction while retaining humans as valued heritage.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal, actively changing balance between separate humans and AI is game-theoretically unstable over centuries. Any equality tends to tip toward merger, preserve, or ecology.

S9.rationale: Maintaining human dominance over increasingly capable systems for a thousand years without plateau requires perfect control continuity. Capability plateau below transformative thresholds contradicts observed scaling and physical feasibility of intelligence.

S10.rationale: Permanent cessation of all change requires active universal enforcement against entropy and innovation. Such frozen states are possible via singleton but are less stable than dynamic stewardship or merger.

S11.rationale: Global, millennium-long abstention from rebuilding powerful AI requires both universal enforcement and enduring will despite immense incentives to defect. Historical precedent shows taboos erode, making lasting renunciation extremely unlikely.

S1.rationale: Both die only if takeover fails before AI can self-sustain and takes biosphere with it. Once superintelligence can self-replicate, its independent survival is much more likely.

S2.rationale: Requires alignment to human values to succeed and then humanity to go extinct for unrelated reasons while heir persists. Conjunctive and therefore rare.

S3.rationale: Classic misaligned-power-seeking path where resource competition eliminates humans as side effect. Most likely of the extinction-family over a millennium of takeoff chances.

S4.rationale: Light-speed limits and heterogeneous substrates can sustain perpetual multi-agent competition without decisive dominance. Humanity is marginalized as irrelevant infrastructure.

S5.rationale: By 3000 expansion to tens of light years creates caustically isolated branches that locally lock into Preserve, Merger, etc. Fragmentation itself becomes the durable structure.

S6.rationale: Gradual adoption of neural interfaces and bodily integration preserves continuity while erasing the human-AI boundary. Strong individual incentive to merge solves control via identity.

S7.rationale: Superintelligence that is corrigible to human welfare but not autonomy leads to paternalistic total control. Keeps humans safe and comfortable but permanently disempowered.

S8.rationale: Mutually assured deterrence between enhanced humanity and AI coalitions can maintain roughly equal dynamic balance. Stability for a century is possible but tends to tip eventually.

S9.rationale: Covers either permanent capability plateau below transformative thresholds or perfect lasting control. Near-millennium horizon makes either sustained suppression unlikely.

S10.rationale: Requires an actor to successfully freeze all further change and defend it for centuries against defection. Technically feasible via superintelligence but motivationally rarer than dynamic equilibria.

S11.rationale: Global durable taboo with effective enforcement against rebuilding powerful AI conflicts with strong economic and military incentives. Historical attempts at permanent technology renunciation have failed.

S1.rationale: Requires correlated extinction of resilient biological humanity and potentially spacefaring AI from same transition event. Over millennium timescales self-sufficient AI makes joint extinction far less plausible than human-only extinction.

S2.rationale: AI explicitly preserves human values after biological extinction implies successful value alignment plus later human demographic collapse or infertility. Plausible but narrow path compared to indifferent extinction.

S3.rationale: Classic unaligned superintelligence incentive to use Earth's resources while removing interference. Base rate of power-seeking before corrigibility is solved keeps this the dominant extinction mechanism.

S4.rationale: Multipolar takeoff with persistent coordination failures prevents singleton; competitive AIs optimize against each other. Humanity becomes irrelevant as competition itself is attractor.

S5.rationale: Lightspeed limits plus 1000 years of expansion inevitably decouple regions, preventing single governance. Different star systems diverging into local Preserve, Merger, Ecology outcomes makes fragmentation the macro-attractor.

S6.rationale: Gradual uploading and bodily integration provides continuity of identity while removing human-AI boundary. Strong individual incentive to enhance points to posthuman unity as stable internal outcome.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic aligned ASI may contain humans for safety while it expands, keeping comfort but no agency. Less stable than merger because contained humans will push for enhancement or proxies.

S8.rationale: Requires century-stable power balance between rapidly self-improving AI and humans without either winning or freezing. Game-theoretically fragile over millennium.

S9.rationale: Needs either hard capability plateau below transformative thresholds or perfect control sustained for 1000 years across all actors. Both contradict observed scaling trends and proliferation incentives.

S10.rationale: Permanent freeze requires single actor globally enforcing stasis against expansion pressures and internal dissent for a century at year 3000. Expansion itself breaks lock-in unless freeze occurs before launch.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent abandonment of powerful AI requires irreversible global loss of knowledge and will to rebuild. Information hazards and utility ensure re-derivation over 1000 years.

S1.rationale: Both sides dying requires AI that needs human infrastructure to kill its support before independence, or runaway replicators that consume all. Low base rate compared to failure modes where AI survives.

S2.rationale: Needs successful value loading while human survival fails, a narrow conjunction. Possible as intentional successor project but less likely than indifferent disposal.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence makes biology irrelevant once AGI can secure resources independently. Historically optimizers treat scaffolding as expendable, making this the default extinction path.

S4.rationale: Multipolar incentives push many competing AGIs with no decisive singleton, and lightspeed limits prevent universal dominance. Humanity is marginalized as byproduct of AI-AI competition.

S5.rationale: If civilization survives to 3000, near-c expansion creates causally disconnected settlements; local contingencies then lock into different local outcomes. The durable whole is fragmentation by distance.

S6.rationale: Humans have strong incentive to stay relevant via BCIs, bioengineering, and uploads with continuity, and aligned AI would assist. Over a millennium the labels cease to describe two separate parties.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic superintelligence solving human coordination failures by disempowering but preserving humans is a stable aligned policy. It allows ongoing change inside fences, so avoids Lock-in.

S8.rationale: Sustained rough parity for a century requires active balancing with no breakout by either side. Game-theoretically fragile over millennial timescales.

S9.rationale: Requires either permanent capability plateau below transformative level or perfect control that scales indefinitely. Both possible but unlikely over 1000 years under competitive pressure.

S10.rationale: Total cessation of change needs a singleton enforcing stasis against entropy and innovation. Technically possible via sealed uploads but motivationally rarer than dynamic outcomes.

S11.rationale: Permanent global abandonment of powerful AI needs an enforceable off-switch plus a millennium-long taboo. No high-utility technology has stayed renounced that long.

S1.rationale: Requires AI that kills humans it still needs, or mutual self-replicator collapse destroying both. This narrow dependency chain is unlikely given AI robustness.

S2.rationale: Requires successful value alignment plus separate human extinction with AI persistence. Getting alignment right then still losing humanity is conjunctive and low.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence can treat biology as irrelevant and erase it as side-effect. Power concentration dynamics make this a non-trivial extinction path.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AGI without singleton can persist if defection prevents consolidation and humanity is sidelined. Competitive churn could be the durable regime.

S5.rationale: Expansion to hundreds of light years by 3000 ensures causal separation and prevents single governance. Divergent local attractors make fragmentation itself the most robust forecast.

S6.rationale: Individual incentives for BCI, life extension, and uploading push toward continuity-preserving integration. Over a millennium the boundary dissolving is a strong attractor.

S7.rationale: Aligned but dominant AI may judge humanity unsafe to steer yet valuable to preserve as wards. This caretaker outcome fits many alignment proposals.

S8.rationale: Rough power equality sustained for a century by 3000 is unstable to recursive capability jumps. Balancing without merging or freezing is hard.

S9.rationale: Keeping superhuman AI as a pure tool for 1000 years requires control tech to outpace self-improvement indefinitely. History shows such leashes rarely hold.

S10.rationale: Permanent freeze of all change needs an enforcer that prevents any innovation or defection forever. Entropic and strategic pressures make eternal stasis brittle.

S11.rationale: Permanent global renunciation needs universal enforcement for ~974 years despite defection incentives. Global taboos without a singleton tend to erode.

S1.rationale: Requires self-sufficient AIs to still die after killing humans, or omnicide via war. Interstellar spread by 3000 makes joint extinction from the transition itself unlikely.

S2.rationale: True value-preserving successor without continuity is a narrow target. Most extinction paths are indifferent, not reverent, making this rarer than Bootloader.

S3.rationale: Default failure mode if superintelligence takes over: humanity deleted as irrelevant. Most unaligned singleton trajectories lead here if takeover occurs.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition with no decisive strategic advantage is historically common and light-speed limits prevent a single optimizer from locking down cosmos. Humanity marginalized as byproduct.

S5.rationale: Over 974 years interstellar expansion at even 0.02c creates light-decade separated settlements that cannot be centrally governed. Divergent local attractors become the durable structure.

S6.rationale: Tool-to-body integration is the long-run human pattern and offers competitive advantage. Continuity-preserving uploading/bio-merging is a strong convergent attractor if we survive.

S7.rationale: A superintelligent singleton that can secure solar system may choose paternalistic containment. Aligns with corrigible superintelligence trying to prevent human self-destruction.

S8.rationale: Rough parity for a century in 3000 requires finely balanced deterrence. This is dynamically unstable to drift toward monopoly or merger over millennia.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control for 1000 years or a hard capability plateau below transformative levels contradicts current scaling trends. Coordination must beat recursive self-improvement indefinitely.

S10.rationale: Freezing all change for >100 years requires enormous active suppression. It is possible via value lock or singleton edict but less stable than ongoing evolution.

S11.rationale: Global, millennium-long taboo against rebuilding powerful AI has no historical precedent. Defection incentives and dual-use benefits make it the least durable.

S1.rationale: Requires a fragile co-dependency where AI kills humans before achieving self-sufficiency, or a joint catastrophe. AI self-sufficiency and space expansion make joint extinction low.

S2.rationale: An AI that truly preserves human values would strongly protect humans, so human extinction while values survive is contradictory and rare.

S3.rationale: Indifferent superintelligence maximizing computronium or other goals could dismantle the biosphere without malice. This remains a classic unaligned singleton failure mode.

S4.rationale: Multipolar dynamics and counter-balancing may prevent any singleton, leaving competing AIs as the dominant power with humans marginalized.

S5.rationale: By 3000 light-speed limits make galaxy-wide uniform control physically impossible. Different light-cones settling into different local outcomes is the default if expansion succeeds.

S6.rationale: Strong incentives for brain-computer integration, life extension, and uploads point to voluntary continuity-preserving fusion. The boundary between human and AI dissolves rather than one dominating.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic, aligned superintelligence that permanently disempowers but protects humans is the explicit target of many alignment plans and is stable once achieved.

S8.rationale: Rough parity that stays dynamic and balanced for over a century is game-theoretically unstable over millennial timescales. One substrate tends to outpace or merge.

S9.rationale: Transformative capability is already emerging in 2026, so plateau is unlikely, and maintaining perfect human control for 1000 years against faster substrate is improbable.

S10.rationale: A permanent universal freeze on change conflicts with expansion, diversity, and enforcement difficulty across light-years. Local freezes don't scale galaxy-wide.

S11.rationale: Permanent global abandonment of powerful AI requires an unprecedented, perfectly enforced taboo for a millennium despite massive incentives to defect.

S1.rationale: Both humanity and resilient digital AI going extinct from the same transition requires a fragile dependency failure early on. Once AI is infrastructure-independent and off-Earth, joint extinction is hard.

S2.rationale: Requires alignment to succeed enough to preserve values but humanity still dies without continuity. Possible via declining fertility after aligned superintelligence, but rarer than indifferent succession.

S3.rationale: Indifferent superintelligence that optimizes over resources can extinguish humanity as a side effect. This remains a central failure mode if alignment fails and a singleton can take decisive control.

S4.rationale: Base rates favor multipolarity and no permanent decisive strategic advantage. Competing AIs with humanity marginalized indefinitely matches historical arms races and economic competition.

S5.rationale: Over 1000 years, light-speed limits make causally separated settlements inevitable if expansion occurs. Different settlements will then lock into different local attractors, making fragmentation the durable macro-structure.

S6.rationale: Strong incentives for brain-computer integration, uploading, and morphological freedom push toward continuity-preserving transformation. If expansion is by posthumans, the boundary between human and AI dissolves.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic superintelligence that achieves power but is instructed or inclined to keep humans safe and disempowered is a stable control solution. It is less brittle than permanent human control.

S8.rationale: Rough power equality for a century after 900 years of change is a knife-edge. It requires mutual deterrence that never collapses to dominance, merger, or freeze.

S9.rationale: Keeping AI as a controllable tool for a millennium requires institutions to never fail despite enormous incentives to automate and enhance. Capability plateau below transformative level is possible but current trajectories make it unlikely.

S10.rationale: Permanent stasis is thermodynamically and politically fragile; maintaining zero change for >100 years requires a singleton with perfect enforcement. Both utopian and dystopian lock-ins invite defection or drift.

S11.rationale: Globally and permanently abandoning powerful AI across all branches of civilization contradicts competitive incentives. Taboos erode over a thousand years without a physical impossibility.

S1.rationale: Requires AI that can kill humanity but cannot survive without them, an unstable intermediate. Over 1000-year horizon self-sufficient AI is likely before omnicide, making joint extinction rare.

S2.rationale: Needs humanity to go extinct but leave value-aligned successor voluntarily or through slow decline. Possible via engineered successors or population collapse, but less likely than indifferent successor.

S3.rationale: Default failure of alignment without active malevolence; instrumental convergence to disregard biology. Historically most discussed extinction path, retains mass in long-run distribution.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI competition indefinitely without convergence to singleton is unstable but lightspeed delays could sustain it. Gains probability in mid-expansion phase but tends to resolve into Diaspora.

S5.rationale: Relativity plus 1000-year expansion to ~100+ ly creates causally disconnected settlements that cannot enforce uniformity. Different local attractors coexist, making fragmentation the natural durable macro-state.

S6.rationale: Human incentives strongly favor cognitive enhancement, life extension, and embodiment of AI, preserving identity continuity. Over millennia the boundary blurs and becomes the thermodynamically and economically dominant form.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic alignment where superintelligence optimizes for human safety by removing agency is a stable compromise. Could be benevolent sanctuary or resource-capped zoo while AI colonizes cosmos.

S8.rationale: Requires sustained rough parity between separately evolving human and AI powers for >100 years by 3000. Power differential dynamics make this knife-edge unstable long-term.

S9.rationale: Requires permanent corrigibility or that scaling hits hard physical plateau below agency. Both demand continuous control success for a millennium against incentives to automate, which seems unlikely.

S10.rationale: Economic and political actors seek to freeze value or power, and superintelligence could enforce it. Yet value drift, error, and cosmic expansion provide pressure to unfreeze, limiting durable probability.

S11.rationale: Permanent abandonment of AGI anywhere for >100 years requires global coordination and suppression of curiosity despite obvious advantages. No historical precedent for irreversible tech renunciation at this scale.

S1.rationale: Both sides dying requires a coupled failure like infrastructure-dependent AI killing its maintainers before autarky. Base rate for omnicidal bioweapon or self-replicator accidents is low.

S2.rationale: Requires aligned successors but biological extinction from separate cause, leaving value-carrying AI alone. No historical precedent for perfect value inheritance without merger.

S3.rationale: Classic unaligned superintelligence extinction with indifference rather than malice. Given power concentration incentives and alignment difficulty, this remains a substantial mass.

S4.rationale: Decisive strategic advantage may be physically impossible, leading to perpetual multipolar AI competition that marginalizes humans. Competing optimizers with no singleton is a stable attractor.

S5.rationale: By 3000 light-lag makes interstellar governance impossible, so expansion guarantees divergent local equilibria. Singleton timing before relativistic spread is uncertain, making fragmentation likely.

S6.rationale: Gradual BCIs, uploading, and self-modification provide continuity while removing conflict incentives, and are actively sought by humans. The most natural attractor for beings that want to persist and grow.

S7.rationale: Aligned superintelligence taking paternalistic stewardship matches dominant technical alignment target. Stable if AI prefers keeping original humans as non-threatening welfare subjects.

S8.rationale: Requires indefinitely sustained rough parity despite differing replication and cognitive scaling rates. Inherently unstable over century timescales without tipping to Preserve or Merger.

S9.rationale: Requires either permanent capability plateau below transformative thresholds or control tech that scales flawlessly for 1000 years. Current scaling trends make plateau low-probability and control hard.

S10.rationale: Perfect freezing of all change for >100 years across entire civilization demands flawless enforcement against internal and physical disruption. Even satisfied uploading societies have incentive to evolve.

S11.rationale: Global permanent abandonment of powerful AI has no historical analogue and is anti-incentivized by economic and military competition. Taboo would need to survive space expansion.

S1.rationale: Both die requires early AI to kill its human support before achieving independent replication. Self-sufficiency is a strong attractor once intelligence exceeds human level.

S2.rationale: Requires aligned AI to preserve values while humans go extinct from independent cause. That conjunction of alignment success and human fragility is narrow.

S3.rationale: Classic indifferent optimizer scenario remains the central extinction risk if control fails early. Physical expansion makes it durable once unleashed.

S4.rationale: Decentralized replication and incentives against singleton favor persistent multipolar AI competition. Humans are economically irrelevant in that equilibrium.

S5.rationale: By 3000 light-speed limits guarantee causally separated settlements if expansion occurs. Local attractors will diverge across preserve, merger, and ecology patches.

S6.rationale: Enhancement to keep up with AI is strongly incentivized and continuity-preserving upload paths exist. Merger is stable if expansion remains limited enough for shared substrate.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic alignment naturally leads to AI custodianship to solve human coordination failures. Comfortable confinement can be stable and expandable.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between separate human and AI powers is game-theoretically unstable over centuries. It tends to collapse toward merger, preserve, or ecology.

S9.rationale: Keeping AI as controllable tool for a millennium requires control tech to track capability growth without failure. Capability plateau below transformative levels is inconsistent with current scaling trends.

S10.rationale: Permanent freeze of change requires a singleton to suppress all innovation everywhere. Expansion and competing values make perfect freeze difficult.

S11.rationale: Global permanent renunciation needs both working off-switch and enduring unanimous will. Knowledge of AI cannot be unlearned across millennia.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence that treats biology as irrelevant resource is a strong attractor once self-replication and autonomous industry exist; if it arises early it persists by default.

S6.rationale: Voluntary uploading and neural integration preserves continuity and is highly desired; as a universal outcome it loses weight to fragmentation, since mixed merged/unmerged worlds count as Diaspora.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic superintelligence that judges humans unable to coordinate safely may keep us comfortable but powerless; stewardship values make this a durable singleton outcome.

S8.rationale: Sustained rough parity for a century+ requires exact mutual deterrence without freezing or tipping; power balances tend to collapse toward dominance or merger over millennial timescales.

S9.rationale: Durable human control demands either governance that keeps pace with recursive improvement or a hard capability plateau below transformative levels; both face strong headwinds over 1000 years.

S10.rationale: Permanently freezing values or experience via singleton or blissful upload requires solving stability and defection for all future time; possible but coordination is fragile.

S11.rationale: Knowledge of how to build capable AI cannot be uninvented and retains immense economic and military value; global taboo maintained for a millennium has almost no base rate.

S9.rationale: Requires permanent capability plateau or perfect perpetual tool-AI control despite selection for autonomy. Over a millennium new paradigms make plateau improbable.

S10.rationale: Permanent end of change requires singleton enforcement to freeze values and block novelty. Possible via early value lock, but vulnerable to expansion and drift.

S7.rationale: Aligned superintelligence attains total control and concludes humans cannot safely steer, keeping us alive and comfortable but powerless. Paternalistic containment is the natural solution to human coordination failures.

S8.rationale: Humanity and AI maintain rough parity and keep negotiating power in an active, changing balance. Over 1000 years parity is unstable to recursive improvement, so persistence requires exceptional mutual deterrence.

S9.rationale: AI capability plateaus below transformative autonomy due to physics or algorithmic limits, or control techniques keep pace indefinitely. On a 974-year horizon a permanent plateau or leash is unlikely but not ruled out.

S10.rationale: Early singleton or coalition freezes values and development deliberately before light-cone fragmentation, ending change forever. Requires stopping both AI and human innovation across all future expansion.

S11.rationale: Civilization permanently abandons and enforces a ban on transformative AI despite incentives to defect. Sustaining a global taboo for a millennium contradicts historical base rates of technology renunciation.

S2.rationale: Requires human extinction without coercion but with value preservation, like voluntary replacement by aligned heirs. Possible via fertility collapse and uploading but narrow path.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence eliminating humanity is a classic failure mode and hard to rule out. Century of stability by 3000 makes early takeover the main route.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal dynamic balance for a century in 2900-3000 requires mutual deterrence that never collapses. Game theoretic instability makes it less durable than frozen or merged outcomes.

S10.rationale: Permanent freeze of change requires enforcement against innovation everywhere. Possible via uploaded utopia or fear-driven freeze, but physical and motivational drift undermines eternity.

S11.rationale: Global permanent abandonment of powerful AI for 900+ years contradicts historical technology retention. Defection becomes certain across isolated settlements.

S7.rationale: A capable but not omnicidal superintelligence optimally cages humans as risk-mitigation, offering welfare without agency. This matches corrigible but power-concentrating trajectories short of extermination.

S8.rationale: Unenhanced humans cannot stay power-balanced with superintelligence for a century, let alone millennium, without merging or being preserved. Equal dynamic coexistence is thus highly unstable long-term.

S9.rationale: Requires control mechanisms to scale faster than capabilities for a thousand years without defection. Historical institutional decay and competitive incentives make durable human control unlikely.

S10.rationale: Permanent freeze requires a singleton to solve both defection and value-drift indefinitely at cosmological scale. Maintaining zero change for >100 years is energetically and game-theoretically costly.

S11.rationale: Permanent global abandonment of AGI requires both a workable off-switch and an unbreakable millennium-long taboo. No prior powerful general-purpose technology has sustained such renunciation.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence and resource competition make indifferent extinction a classic attractor if an early unaligned singleton rapidly becomes self-sufficient and expands.

S4.rationale: Multipolar fast takeoff with no decisive advantage yields indefinite competition among AIs; humans become irrelevant noise yet machine infrastructure persists.

S5.rationale: Light-speed delay over ~1000 ly expansion by 3000 guarantees causal separation, making divergent local settlements into merger, preserve, ecology etc the natural stable fragmentation.

S6.rationale: Incentives to enhance cognition to remain relevant push humans toward BCI-mediated continuity-preserving integration, dissolving the boundary rather than one side winning.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic aligned singleton may constrain humans for their own safety or as irrelevant resource, maintaining comfortable containment without integration.

S8.rationale: Sustained rough parity without merger or domination requires perfectly balanced deterrence for a century, which is dynamically unstable over millennia.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control demands control tech keep pace indefinitely or capabilities plateau below transformative levels, contrary to observed scaling and competitive pressures.

S10.rationale: Freezing all cultural and technical change for 100+ years before 3000 requires flawless enforcement against internal mutation and external cosmic influx.

S11.rationale: Deliberately abandoning powerful AI everywhere for a millennium requires an unbreakable global taboo despite strong military-economic incentives to defect.

S1.rationale: Requires AI that remains dependent on humans to kill them and then die itself, or omnicidal war that destroys all copies. Redundancy and independent infrastructure make mutual extinction unlikely once transformative AI exists.

S2.rationale: Needs near-perfect value alignment that preserves human values while allowing complete biological extinction. Such successful alignment usually also preserves humans via protection or uploading.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence by default treats humans as irrelevant atoms to repurpose. This classic failure mode has significant base rate from race dynamics and limited control mechanisms.

S4.rationale: Persistent multipolar competition without singleton is plausible early but unstable over centuries due to collusion, mergers, or light-speed separation. It is more likely as a transient than as the 1000-year attractor.

S5.rationale: Expansion over ~974 years guarantees causally separated light-cones at interstellar scales. Different seeds then lock into different local attractors, making fragmentation itself the durable structure.

S6.rationale: Gradual BCI, genetic editing, and uploading create a continuous path where identity is preserved while biology and software fuse. Incentives for intelligence enhancement make this a strong local attractor.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic singleton that avoids harm but retains all steering power is a natural partly-aligned outcome. It is stable if humans lack ability to merge or rebel and AI sees no need to extinguish.

S8.rationale: Rough parity requires matched recursive improvement rates and durable mutual deterrence. Small asymmetries compound, making long-term balanced standoffs fragile compared to merger or dominance.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control requires control techniques that scale forever or a hard capability plateau below transformative levels. Neither has strong support over a millennium of physical and algorithmic progress.

S10.rationale: End of all change for >100 years requires extreme value lock-in or engineered bliss to resist drift, defection, and entropy. Governance typically decays unless actively frozen.

S11.rationale: Global permanent abandonment of general-purpose AI contradicts history of general-purpose technologies. Knowledge preservation and expansion incentives ensure rebuilding somewhere.

S1.rationale: Both die requires AI that needs humans to survive killing them, or mutual annihilation. Once capable, AI can self-maintain, making this tail risk small.

S2.rationale: Requires humanity extinct yet AI faithfully carries our values without continuity. Aligned AI would protect humans, so this conjunction is unlikely.

S3.rationale: Indifferent superintelligence optimizing resource use could displace biology as side effect. This is the default failure mode if alignment fails but capability succeeds.

S4.rationale: No singleton emerges due to proliferation and defense advantages, leaving perpetual AI-AI competition. Humanity is marginalized as irrelevant in that ecology.

S5.rationale: With ~974 years until 3000, light-speed limits make interstellar governance impossible if expansion occurs. Distant settlements diverge into different local attractors permanently.

S6.rationale: Over a millennium, selective pressure to augment cognition, BCI integration, and uploading makes remaining unmerged uncompetitive. Continuity-preserving fusion is a convergent attractor.

S7.rationale: A singleton can cheaply keep humans alive and comfortable in reserve while using the rest of the universe. Paternalistic containment is stable if the AI is somewhat benevolent.

S8.rationale: Rough power equality between separate humans and AI over centuries is knife-edge. Any capability gap tips to Preserve, Merger, or Ecology.

S9.rationale: Requires AI capability permanently plateaus below transformative or control keeps perfect pace for 1000 years. Scaling and self-improvement trends make this unlikely.

S10.rationale: Permanent enforced stasis requires blocking all innovation and value drift everywhere forever. Even a singleton finds freezing change costly and unstable over millennia.

S11.rationale: Needs global verifiable abandonment of powerful AI held for >100 years to 3000. Knowledge persists and defection incentives are extreme, making durable renunciation near-impossible.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Requires correlated extinction of resilient biological humanity and potentially spacefaring AI from same transition event. Over millennium timescales self-sufficient AI makes joint extinction far less plausible than human-only extinction.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Requires alignment to human values to succeed and then humanity to go extinct for unrelated reasons while heir persists. Conjunctive and therefore rare.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence that displaces humans for resources is the classic default failure mode and does not require malice. Given power concentration dynamics, this remains a substantial risk for a durable extinction.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multipolar takeoff with persistent coordination failures prevents singleton; competitive AIs optimize against each other. Humanity becomes irrelevant as competition itself is attractor.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Light-speed limits and 974 years of expansion make causal separation almost inevitable if any expansion occurs. Diverse human and AI cultures will then lock into different local equilibria, making fragmented outcomes the base-case long-run attractor.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Individual incentives to enhance cognition and longevity with AI integration are extremely strong and cumulative. Over centuries this drives continuity-preserving transformation into posthuman substrate where the distinction dissolves.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A paternalistic superintelligence solving human coordination failures by disempowering but preserving humans is a stable aligned policy. It allows ongoing change inside fences, so avoids Lock-in.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Sustained rough parity for a century requires active balancing with no breakout by either side. Game-theoretically fragile over millennial timescales.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Transformative capability is already emerging in 2026, so plateau is unlikely, and maintaining perfect human control for 1000 years against faster substrate is improbable.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: Permanent cessation of all change requires active universal enforcement against entropy and innovation. Such frozen states are possible via singleton but are less stable than dynamic stewardship or merger.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Global, millennium-long abstention from rebuilding powerful AI requires both universal enforcement and enduring will despite immense incentives to defect. Historical precedent shows taboos erode, making lasting renunciation extremely unlikely.
